attributes.reverted_gworldinfo_subattempt: Separately attempted a TU-wide gWorldInfo/WorldInfo header consolidation (include/game/worldinfo.h already exists with a full GC-verified WorldInfo struct - the file's own top-of-file comment claiming 'no worldinfo.h exists in this tree' is STALE) across fn_8005ACE0/fn_8005AF98/fn_8005E90C/fn_8005BA1C/fn_8005C1DC/fn_8005D730/fn_800606FC (15 sites using 3 duplicate local `extern u8 gWorldInfo[]` declarations plus a redundant GauntWorldInfoView typedef) - iteminfo/iteminfodata (already in game/item.h) fully explains fn_8005BA1C's/fn_8005C1DC's `rec`-walked iteminfo-array records (type/subtype/desc/value fields all matched exactly). Converting the base-pointer expressions to `(u8*)&gWorldInfo + offsetof(WorldInfo,field)` regressed fn_8005BA1C (real 529->615, STRUCTURAL) AND, independently, an untouched sibling fn_8005FDA8 (real 16->62) - a whole-TU constant-pool coupling effect. Root cause isolated and FULLY explained (not a fundamental blocker): a mechanical `replace_all` unified all four `niteminfos`-bound loop headers in fn_8005BA1C onto the block-local `world` pointer, but the ORIGINAL source used `world+0x74` at 2 sites and the bare `gWorldInfo+0x74` directly at the other 2 despite identical values - restoring the exact per-site spelling fixed BOTH regressions simultaneously. This is now a fully-diagnosed, low-risk-to-redo opportunity (see the companion law), but was left REVERTED this session rather than re-attempted, because 2 of the 7 touched functions are register-allocation-sensitive and close to matching (fn_8005D730 fuzzy 99.35% PARKED at REGISTER_ONLY/SCHEDULE; fn_8005C1DC has an active REGISTER_ONLY improved-attempt) and re-verifying per-site spelling safely for all 15 sites plus a full-TU gate after each would cost more of this session's budget than the primarily-documentation-value win justified.
